edbDesc: A change in optical absorption by a semiconductor when an electric field is applied. Used to create electroabsorption modulators.
title: Electroabsorption
description: A thin layer of semiconductor that normally lets a laser beam through starts to swallow it when a few volts are applied across it. Walter Franz in Germany and Leonid Keldysh in Moscow predicted it independently in 1958. Because it switches in trillionths of a second, it is used to flick laser light on and off to send internet data down optical fibres.
effect: an electric field makes a semiconductor absorb light it used to let through
strength: A couple of volts can block most of a beam, and it switches tens of billions of times a second.
pickWhy: Specific effect with a clear job; named Electroabsorption, the broader common term that covers the Franz-Keldysh effect.
